causal_claim.content: Rigid, inelastic resin materials prevent reliance on deformable active flow-control components.
causal_claim.evidence_span: As a result, 3D-printed microfluidic devices often cannot rely on deformable components for active flow control and must instead achieve functionality primarily through the careful design of internal geometries and fluidic pathways.

causal_claim.content: Dependence on geometry increases demands on precise design coordination.
causal_claim.evidence_span: This strong dependence on geometry places greater demands on the design process: channel lengths, volumes, resistances, and timing relationships must be coordinated precisely to ensure correct fluid handling, synchronized reactions, and accurate dispensing behavior [13].

causal_claim.content: Light penetration and scattering cause over-curing outside intended regions.
causal_claim.evidence_span: During printing, light penetration and scattering can cause polymerization outside the intended exposure region, a phenomenon commonly referred to as over-curing.

causal_claim.content: Over-curing introduces geometric deviations and can block channels.
causal_claim.evidence_span: This effect introduces geometric deviations from the nominal design and is especially problematic in narrow channels and in fine, complex internal features. In severe cases, over-curing can partially or completely block channels, rendering a device unusable.

causal_claim.content: High-end printers may reduce inaccuracies but undermine affordability.
causal_claim.evidence_span: High-end printers may alleviate some of these problems, but they do so at the expense of affordability, thereby weakening one of the most compelling motivations for using 3D printing in the first place.

causal_claim.content: Integrating design support, constraint-driven synthesis, and ML-assisted compensation lowers barriers for non-experts and reduces development time and cost.
causal_claim.evidence_span: By integrating interactive design support, constraint-driven functional synthesis, and machine-learning-assisted manufacturing compensation, the presented methodologies lower the barrier to entry for non-expert users and reduce the time and cost required to develop complex microfluidic systems.

causal_claim.content: UV light penetration and scattering cause unintended polymerization in trapped resin inside microchannels.
causal_claim.evidence_span: This phenomenon, known as light penetration or over-curing, causes unintended polymerization of the residual liquid resin trapped inside the microchannels.

causal_claim.content: Cumulative UV exposure distorts dimensions, changes hydraulic resistance, and can clog channels.
causal_claim.evidence_span: This cumulative UV exposure severely distorts the fabricated dimensions of the features, altering their intended hydraulic resistance and, in extreme cases, completely clogging the fluidic pathways

causal_claim.content: Parameterized components enable rapid iteration and reduce invalid geometries.
causal_claim.evidence_span: This approach encapsulates domain knowledge directly into the design representation, enabling rapid iteration and reducing the likelihood of invalid geometries.

causal_claim.content: The platform shifts design from geometric modeling to configuration of functional building blocks.
causal_claim.evidence_span: As a result, the platform shifts the design task from geometric modeling to the configuration and composition of microfluidic functionality.

causal_claim.content: Introducing calibrated volume offsets produces prescribed delay differences under assigned flow conditions.
causal_claim.evidence_span: shifted-arrival constraints are implemented by introducing calibrated volume offsets that produce prescribed delay differences under the assigned flow conditions.

causal_claim.evidence_span: In this way, routing decisions directly influence whether temporal objectives are satisfied.

mechanism_principle.content: Because common resins are rigid and inelastic, unlike PDMS, they cannot support elastic active elements.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Off-the-shelf materials for resin printing generally produce rigid and inelastic structures, in contrast to PDMS-based devices, which can exploit the elasticity of the substrate to implement active elements such as pneumatic valves and pumps.

mechanism_principle.content: Light penetration depth follows Beer-Lambert exponential decay, while neighboring features reflect, refract, and scatter light.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: The extent of this light penetration depth is governed by the Beer-Lambert law, which dictates an exponential decay of light intensity as it travels through the resin. Neighboring structural features also reflect, refract, and scatter this light, creating localized variations in the over-curing effect.

mechanism_principle.content: In passive chips, geometry directly encodes functional correctness.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: In passive chips, this challenge is particularly acute because functional correctness is encoded directly in geometry.

mechanism_principle.content: Under laminar-flow assumptions, geometry is coupled to behavior via resistance-flow relations and T=V/Q.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Under laminar-flow assumptions, 3M-DeSyn couples geometry to behavior using resistance- and flow-based relationships, together with a volume-to-time relation (T = V/Q).

mechanism_principle.content: Concentration control in passive reagent preparation depends on maintaining robust volume ratios without active valves or pumps.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: This is particularly important for passive reagent preparation, where concentration control depends on maintaining robust volume ratios without active valves or pumps.

mechanism_principle.content: Distributing and reordering subcomponents increases distinct laminar sub-streams, supporting better passive homogenization.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Intuitively, by distributing and reordering subcomponents in the tree, the outlet can exhibit more distinct laminar sub-streams (referred to as wider spectrum width), which supports better passive homogenization after merging.

mechanism_principle.content: Because passive systems lack active perturbation, flow ordering and geometric interleaving are key for mixing performance.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: This is an important design choice because passive systems cannot rely on active perturbation; therefore, flow ordering and geometric interleaving become key levers for practical mixing performance.

mechanism_principle.content: Under common pressure, resistive channel paths enforce intended relative flow rates so outlet composition matches the target ratio.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Under a common pressure boundary, these resistive paths enforce the intended relative flow rates so that outlet composition tracks the original target ratio.

mechanism_principle.content: Local and global compensation address different causes of over-curing: depth-varying dose versus nearby-void polymerization risk.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span:
This local-plus-global decomposition provides a flexible mecha-
nism: local compensation addresses depth-dependent exposure
nonuniformity, while global compensation provides additional
robustness for difficult print settings.

mechanism_principle.content: Local compensation is based on exponential light attenuation with distance.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span:
Local compensation is
derived from a Beer–Lambert-style attenuation assumption in
which light intensity decays exponentially with distance from
the source.

mechanism_principle.content: Preprocessing incorporates light-propagation physics so the model sees physically meaningful context.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span:
Specifically, geometric features are weighted
based on cumulative light passage and attenuation effects
(including absorption/scattering-related decay), so the model
receives physically meaningful context instead of only raw
geometric descriptors.

hypothesis_statement.content: A unified framework spanning design and fabrication can lower barriers, time, and cost for 3D-printed microfluidics.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: To address these challenges, this paper presents a cohesive design automation framework for 3D-printed microfluidics that unifies a series of interconnected methods across design and fabrication.

hypothesis_statement.content: A web-based interactive platform tailored to 3D-printed microfluidics can overcome infrastructure bottlenecks.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: To overcome these infrastructural bottlenecks, we developed a foundational web-based interactive design automation platform—Flui3d—specifically tailored for 3D-printed microfluidics [15].

hypothesis_statement.content: 3M-DeSyn addresses the joint synthesis problem for multilayer 3D-printed microfluidics.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: To address this problem, we introduced 3M-DeSyn [16].

hypothesis_statement.content: The method shifts complexity from hardware control to algorithmic design synthesis.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: This framing intentionally shifts complexity from hardware control to algorithmic design synthesis.

hypothesis_statement.content: Integrated DFM compensation in Flui3d can enable reliable fabrication on hobby-grade printers without custom materials or hardware changes.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: We introduced practical Design-for-Manufacturing (DFM) compensation strategies that is integrated directly into the design-output stage of Flui3d, enabling reliable fabrication on hobby-grade SLA/LCD platforms without requiring custom resins or printer hardware modifications.

hypothesis_statement.content: The DFM module treats fabrication fidelity as a first-class objective by transforming geometry before export to counter over-curing.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: The DFM module therefore treats fabrication fidelity as a first-class design objective: before STL export, the geometry is transformed to counter expected light-induced over-curing.

hypothesis_statement.content: The goal of DFM compensation is to preserve voids and keep microchannels open after printing, especially in compact vertically integrated devices.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: The goal is to preserve intended void regions and keep microchannels open after printing, especially in compact and vertically integrated devices.

evidence_result.content: A three-layer mixing device can be taken to print-ready design in under five minutes.
evidence_result.evidence_span: For example, the three-layer mixing device from Figure 1 could be taken from initial setup to a print-ready design in less than five minutes, demonstrating the efficiency of this interaction model.

evidence_result.content: 3M-DeSyn reduced design time from hours to seconds or minutes compared with manual workflows.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Compared with a manual baseline workflow (schematic analysis, iterative placement/routing, and hand-tuned channel dimensions), 3M-DeSyn reduced design time from hours to seconds/minutes: baseline estimates ranged from 5 h 07 m to 20 h 54 m, whereas 3M-DeSyn completed synthesis in 2 s to 3 m 40 s.

evidence_result.content: Synthesized chips were fabricated on a low-cost hobby SLA setup, confirming printability of generated geometries.

evidence_result.content: Simulated outlet concentrations were very close to target values across evaluated cases.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Across the four real-world scenarios, simulated outlet concentrations deviated by less than 0.01 mol/L from target values. Over all eight cases, reported deviations remained small (from −0.016 to +0.009 mol/L), while synthesis runtime stayed in the millisecond range (108–145 ms).

evidence_result.evidence_span: Chip footprints and total channel lengths remained moderate relative to a custom baseline, highlighting that µ-MM achieves an effective balance: slightly narrower mixing spectrum in some cases, but substantially improved compactness and manufacturability with lower channel complexity and hydraulic burden.

problem_motivation.content: Despite advances that make 3D printing more accessible for microfluidics, practical adoption and broader dissemination remain limited because designing reliable 3D-printed microfluidic devices is still difficult; persistent challenges in design complexity, functional synthesis, material limitations, fabrication fidelity, and reliable manufacturability create a gap between the promise of low-cost 3D printing and the needs of dependable microfluidic development.
evidence_spans: However, despite these advances in manufacturing, the design of 3D-printed microfluidic systems remains a major challenge.

Overall, this work helps bridge the gap between the accessibility of low-cost 3D printing and the practical requirements of reliable microfluidic device development.

evidence_spans: During printing, light penetration and scattering can cause polymerization outside the intended exposure region, a phenomenon commonly referred to as over-curing.

This effect introduces geometric deviations from the nominal design and is especially problematic in narrow channels and in fine, complex internal features. In severe cases, over-curing can partially or completely block channels, rendering a device unusable.
This phenomenon, known as light penetration or over-curing, causes unintended polymerization of the residual liquid resin trapped inside the microchannels.
This cumulative UV exposure severely distorts the fabricated dimensions of the features, altering their intended hydraulic resistance and, in extreme cases, completely clogging the fluidic pathways

causal_claim.content: High-end printers may reduce fabrication inaccuracies, but only at the cost of affordability, undermining a key motivation for using 3D printing.
evidence_spans: High-end printers may alleviate some of these problems, but they do so at the expense of affordability, thereby weakening one of the most compelling motivations for using 3D printing in the first place.

causal_claim.content: Integrating interactive design support, constraint-driven synthesis, mixer design, and machine-learning-assisted manufacturing compensation lowers barriers for non-experts, reduces development time, cost, and manual effort, and improves print reliability.
evidence_spans: By integrating interactive design support, constraint-driven functional synthesis, and machine-learning-assisted manufacturing compensation, the presented methodologies lower the barrier to entry for non-expert users and reduce the time and cost required to develop complex microfluidic systems.

By combining interactive design support,
constraint-driven synthesis for passive fluidic functions, low-
cost mixer synthesis, and compensation methods for light-
penetration artifacts, the framework reduces manual effort
while improving print reliability on resin 3D printers.

causal_claim.content: Encapsulating domain knowledge in parameterized functional components enables rapid iteration, reduces invalid geometries, and shifts microfluidic design from low-level geometric modeling to configuration and composition of functional building blocks.
evidence_spans: This approach encapsulates domain knowledge directly into the design representation, enabling rapid iteration and reducing the likelihood of invalid geometries.
As a result, the platform shifts the design task from geometric modeling to the configuration and composition of microfluidic functionality.

causal_claim.content: Introducing calibrated volume offsets produces prescribed delay differences under assigned flow conditions, and routing decisions therefore directly determine whether temporal objectives are satisfied.
evidence_spans: shifted-arrival constraints are implemented by introducing calibrated volume offsets that produce prescribed delay differences under the assigned flow conditions.
In this way, routing decisions directly influence whether temporal objectives are satisfied.

causal_claim.content: Ratio decomposition increases flexibility in flow allocation and exposes degrees of freedom for arranging mixing patterns while preserving exact aggregate ratios.
evidence_spans: Decomposition increases flexibility in flow allocation: each reagent contribution can be represented by multiple sub-streams that are later interleaved spatially. This strategy allows the method to preserve exact aggregate ratio contributions while exposing additional degrees of freedom for improving the downstream mixing pattern.

causal_claim.content: Using dynamic, spatially resolved compensation offsets allows deeper, more vulnerable, or otherwise high-risk regions to receive stronger correction automatically, while lower-risk regions receive milder correction.
evidence_spans:
In practice, this allows deeper or more vulnerable
regions to receive stronger compensation automatically, which
is particularly useful for multi-layer channel stacks.

Unlike uniform com-
pensation, this allows stronger correction where local over-
curing risk is high and milder correction where risk is lower.

mechanism_principle.content: Common resin-printed materials are typically rigid and inelastic, unlike PDMS, so they cannot exploit substrate elasticity to realize active elements such as pneumatic valves and pumps; consequently, passive chips must rely on geometry to encode function, including maintaining robust volume ratios for concentration control without active actuation.
evidence_spans: Off-the-shelf materials for resin printing generally produce rigid and inelastic structures, in contrast to PDMS-based devices, which can exploit the elasticity of the substrate to implement active elements such as pneumatic valves and pumps.
In passive chips, this challenge is particularly acute because functional correctness is encoded directly in geometry.
This is particularly important for passive reagent preparation, where concentration control depends on maintaining robust volume ratios without active valves or pumps.

mechanism_principle.content: Under laminar-flow assumptions and a common pressure boundary, device geometry determines behavior through resistance- and flow-based relations together with the volume-to-time relation T = V/Q; resistive channel paths thereby enforce intended relative flow rates so outlet composition matches the target ratio.
evidence_spans: Under laminar-flow assumptions, 3M-DeSyn couples geometry to behavior using resistance- and flow-based relationships, together with a volume-to-time relation (T = V/Q).
Under a common pressure boundary, these resistive paths enforce the intended relative flow rates so that outlet composition tracks the original target ratio.

mechanism_principle.content: Because passive systems lack active perturbation, mixing performance depends on flow ordering and geometric interleaving; distributing and reordering subcomponents increases the number of distinct laminar sub-streams ('wider spectrum width'), which supports better passive homogenization after merging.
evidence_spans: This is an important design choice because passive systems cannot rely on active perturbation; therefore, flow ordering and geometric interleaving become key levers for practical mixing performance.

Intuitively, by distributing and reordering subcomponents in the tree, the outlet can exhibit more distinct laminar sub-streams (referred to as wider spectrum width), which supports better passive homogenization after merging.

mechanism_principle.content: Over-curing and exposure nonuniformity are governed by light-propagation physics: light intensity decays exponentially with depth according to a Beer–Lambert-style law, while neighboring features reflect, refract, and scatter light, creating localized variations; accordingly, local compensation targets depth-dependent attenuation/exposure variation, and global compensation adds robustness for difficult print settings and nearby-void polymerization risks.
evidence_spans: The extent of this light penetration depth is governed by the Beer-Lambert law, which dictates an exponential decay of light intensity as it travels through the resin. Neighboring structural features also reflect, refract, and scatter this light, creating localized variations in the over-curing effect.

This local-plus-global decomposition provides a flexible mechanism: local compensation addresses depth-dependent exposure nonuniformity, while global compensation provides additional robustness for difficult print settings.
Local compensation is derived from a Beer–Lambert-style attenuation assumption in which light intensity decays exponentially with distance from the source.

mechanism_principle.content: Preprocessing incorporates light-propagation physics, including cumulative light passage and attenuation from absorption/scattering, so the model receives physically meaningful context rather than only raw geometric descriptors.
evidence_spans: Specifically, geometric features are weighted based on cumulative light passage and attenuation effects (including absorption/scattering-related decay), so the model receives physically meaningful context instead of only raw geometric descriptors.

hypothesis_statement.content: A unified design-and-fabrication automation framework for 3D-printed microfluidics—implemented as the web-based platform Flui3d—can overcome infrastructure bottlenecks and lower barriers, time, and cost.
evidence_spans: To address these challenges, this paper presents a cohesive design automation framework for 3D-printed microfluidics that unifies a series of interconnected methods across design and fabrication.
To overcome these infrastructural bottlenecks, we developed a foundational web-based interactive design automation platform—Flui3d—specifically tailored for 3D-printed microfluidics [15].

hypothesis_statement.content: 3M-DeSyn addresses the joint synthesis problem for multilayer 3D-printed microfluidics, shifting complexity from hardware control to algorithmic design synthesis.
evidence_spans: To address this problem, we introduced 3M-DeSyn [16].
This framing intentionally shifts complexity from hardware control to algorithmic design synthesis.

hypothesis_statement.content: Integrated DFM compensation in Flui3d treats fabrication fidelity as a first-class objective by transforming geometry before export to counter over-curing, with the goal of preserving voids and keeping microchannels open, thereby enabling reliable fabrication on hobby-grade printers without custom materials or hardware changes.
evidence_spans: We introduced practical Design-for-Manufacturing (DFM) compensation strategies that is integrated directly into the design-output stage of Flui3d, enabling reliable fabrication on hobby-grade SLA/LCD platforms without requiring custom resins or printer hardware modifications.
The DFM module therefore treats fabrication fidelity as a first-class design objective: before STL export, the geometry is transformed to counter expected light-induced over-curing.
The goal is to preserve intended void regions and keep microchannels open after printing, especially in compact and vertically integrated devices.

evidence_result.content: 3M-DeSyn greatly reduced design time versus manual workflows, taking designs from initial setup to print-ready in seconds to minutes; for example, a three-layer mixing device could be made print-ready in under five minutes, compared with manual estimates of 5 h 07 m to 20 h 54 m.
evidence_spans: For example, the three-layer mixing device from Figure 1 could be taken from initial setup to a print-ready design in less than five minutes, demonstrating the efficiency of this interaction model.

Compared with a manual baseline workflow (schematic analysis, iterative placement/routing, and hand-tuned channel dimensions), 3M-DeSyn reduced design time from hours to seconds/minutes: baseline estimates ranged from 5 h 07 m to 20 h 54 m, whereas 3M-DeSyn completed synthesis in 2 s to 3 m 40 s.

evidence_result.content: Synthesized chips were successfully fabricated on a low-cost hobby SLA printer, confirming that the automatically generated geometries were practically printable.
evidence_spans: The synthesized chips were additionally fabricated on a low-cost hobby SLA setup (Anycubic Photon D2 with plant-based clear resin), confirming that the automatically generated geometries are not only computationally valid but also practically printable.

evidence_result.content: Across evaluated mixing cases, simulated outlet concentrations closely matched target values, with deviations below 0.01 mol/L in four real-world scenarios and ranging overall from −0.016 to +0.009 mol/L, while synthesis runtime remained in the millisecond range.
evidence_spans: Across the four real-world scenarios, simulated outlet concentrations deviated by less than 0.01 mol/L from target values. Over all eight cases, reported deviations remained small (from −0.016 to +0.009 mol/L), while synthesis runtime stayed in the millisecond range (108–145 ms).

evidence_result.content: µ-MM achieved a favorable tradeoff between performance and fabrication practicality: although the mixing spectrum was slightly narrower in some cases, chip footprints and total channel lengths stayed moderate relative to a custom baseline, yielding improved compactness, manufacturability, lower channel complexity, and lower hydraulic burden.
evidence_spans: Chip footprints and total channel lengths remained moderate relative to a custom baseline, highlighting that µ-MM achieves an effective balance: slightly narrower mixing spectrum in some cases, but substantially improved compactness and manufacturability with lower channel complexity and hydraulic burden.

evidence_result.content: For fabrication-compensation learning, the dataset comprised 2,488 supervised examples derived from measured fabrication discrepancies.
evidence_spans: This produced 2,488 data points, providing supervised targets for compensation learning.

evidence_result.content: The compensation model converged quickly and generalized stably, reaching convergence in fewer than 40 epochs, about 90.01% training accuracy, and low test error with all reported L1 errors below 0.45 and an average around 0.11.

constraint.content: Designs must satisfy coordinated spatial, hydraulic, and timing constraints: channel lengths, volumes, resistances, and timing relationships must be precisely matched, while placement, routing, non-overlap, layer usage, and filling/flow constraints are simultaneously enforced to ensure correct operation.
evidence_spans: channel lengths, volumes, resistances, and timing relationships must be coordinated precisely to ensure correct fluid handling, synchronized reactions, and accurate dispensing behavior [13].
Designers must simultaneously satisfy spatial constraints—such as placement, routing, non-overlap, and layer usage—and hydraulic constraints, including flow, timing, and filling volume.

constraint.content: Additional manufacturability constraints require sufficient spacing, prevent overlap among components and channels, and guarantee legal inter-layer transitions.
evidence_spans: Additional constraints enforce manufacturable spacing, prevent overlap among components and channels, and guarantee legal inter-layer transitions.
